2. The geostrategic view: Iran as a “mandatory hub”

  • A unique position: the only country with access both to the Caspian Sea (connecting to Russia/Central Asia) and to the Indian Ocean (Persian Gulf + Chabahar).
  • Reducing dependence on the Strait of Hormuz: Chabahar + Bandar Abbas = a strategic solution for India and China in geopolitical crises.
  • Role in China's BRI: Iran could become the alternative to Pakistan in the western section of the “Belt and Road” — especially given Pakistan's political instability.

🌍 Iran is not an option but a strategic necessity for many regional powers.

3. The competitive view: the corridor battleground

While Iran works on the North–South corridor, regional rivals are also active:
Iraq–Turkey–Europe Iraq, Turkey, European Union Proximity to Europe, Mediterranean ports Iraq's internal insecurity, dependence on Turkey
China–Red Sea–Jordan–Mediterranean China, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Israel Chinese capital, advanced technology Political tensions, high cost
Oman–Kuwait–Iraq (southern axis) Oman, Kuwait, Iraq Gulf access, deep-water ports No connection to Central Asia
Pakistan–Chabahar–Afghanistan (Chinese) China, Pakistan Chinese investment ($60 billion) Insecurity, corruption, one-sided dependence on China

✅ Iran's competitive advantage:

  • Two-way connectivity (north + south) — rivals have only one direction.
  • Existing rail infrastructure (12,000+ km of railway) — no need to build from scratch.
  • Domestic retrofit technology — an 80% cost reduction compared to rivals.
